intro: A descent direction’s slope and curvature play different roles. For a quadratic objective they can be computed and checked exactly.
task: Return the objective value, directional slope, directional curvature, and unconstrained minimizing step along the direction.
requirements: hessian is a symmetric square matrix (absolute symmetry tolerance 1e-10); point and direction are matching vectors. Require direction.T@hessian@direction >=1e-8. Average H with H.T after symmetry validation.
For q(x)=0.5*x.T@H@x, return {"value": q(x), "slope": d.T@H@x, "curvature": d.T@H@d, "step": -slope/curvature}. The step is allowed to be negative.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: One dimensional descent
examples.output:
{'value': 9.0, 'slope': -6.0, 'curvature': 2.0, 'step': 3.0}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: One dimensional uphill
examples.output:
{'value': 9.0, 'slope': 6.0, 'curvature': 2.0, 'step': -3.0}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Two-dimensional line
examples.output:
{'value': 9.0, 'slope': -10.0, 'curvature': 6.0, 'step': 1.66666666667}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Expand q(x+t*d) as a quadratic in the scalar t.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Only positive curvature along this direction is required; the matrix need not be positive definite in every direction.

explanation: The slope determines the immediate tendency and curvature describes how that tendency changes along the chosen line. A positive directional curvature gives a unique line minimum.

This is an exact diagnostic for the supplied quadratic, not a finite-difference estimator or a guarantee for a nonlinear network far from the current point. Negative optimal steps simply indicate the selected direction points uphill initially.
